title: Cold rebuild: an HTTPRoute
summary: Write a Gateway API HTTPRoute on a real Kubernetes cluster, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *DNS and Gateways* you routed a host and two paths to two Services with a Gateway API
`HTTPRoute`, on a real cluster. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**.
The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old YAML feels like knowing it; writing
it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson, then come back and try
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A pod in namespace `blog` must call Service `auth` in namespace `identity`. Which URL works?
steps.explain: Short names only resolve in your own namespace. Add `.identity` (or use the full name).

steps.title: An HTTPRoute, cold
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). It has the Gateway API CRDs and the Gateway `public` in
Apply an `HTTPRoute` named `shop` in `shop`, attached to `public`, for `shop.example.com`: paths starting with `/api`
go to the Service `api` on port 80, everything else to `web` on port 80.
From memory: no hints this time.
